operations_plan.summary: Identify and remove the black Cordholder component in the open recessed area while preserving the power cord, plug, cord exit, and unrelated brewing hardware.

steps.description: Resolve the Cordholder identity before editing. First inspect assembly/component names and solid visibility for an object named Cordholder. If no name is available, isolate the black retaining bracket visible in the open recessed region. The most likely model correspondence is S1/F5, upper flow guide, solid 12, faces 296-307 because it is a separate narrow stepped component in that region. S2/F12, solid 7, and S2/F9, solid 4, are secondary visual candidates and must not be removed unless isolation confirms that one of them is the requested Cordholder. Do not classify S5/F19 or S5/F20 as the holder because those are the required cord and plug.

Suppress or delete the confirmed Cordholder component as a complete solid. If identification confirms the expected S1/F5 candidate, remove solid 12 without modifying the surrounding main shell. If the holder is fused into another solid, remove only its generating feature or use a delete-face-and-heal operation on its attachment faces; do not fill or alter the intentional open recess.

Verify that the flexible power cord and molded two-pin plug remain unchanged and connected at the enclosure exit. Confirm that solids 18 and 19, including the housing-side cord end face 393 and cord-to-housing transition face 375, were not deleted, shortened, or detached. Also check that removal did not affect the vessel, internal cylindrical chamber, or fascia supports.

operations_plan.summary: Create a second copy of the existing black U-shaped handle/stand at the opposite longitudinal end of the enclosure, matching the existing stand's profile, orientation, attachment geometry, and offset from the adjacent end wall.

steps.description: Use S4/F18, U-shaped external cradle, solid 17, as the source stand. Establish the enclosure longitudinal datum from the front and rear end closure faces of the main shell, S1/F1 faces 45 and 46. Construct a center plane halfway between those parallel end faces and normal to the enclosure longitudinal axis. Measure the existing stand station from its nearest end wall using the broad cradle faces 368 and 370; this measured end-wall offset is the relational placement constraint for the new stand. This adopts the interpretation that 'other side' means the opposite longitudinal end, since F18 already spans both lateral sides of the housing.

Create an associative mirrored copy of the complete F18 stand solid across the longitudinal center plane from OP2_STEP1. Keep it as a separate solid and new support feature in section S4. The mirrored copy must retain the source thickness, U-shaped inner and outer profiles, arm lengths, pivot bosses, mounting-hole arrangement, and orientation. The mirror relationship places it at approximately the same distance from the opposite end wall as the existing stand is from its adjacent end wall.

Create the receiving attachment interfaces for the new stand by mirroring the existing left and right pivot-seat/bore geometry at the same center plane. Use S1/F1 faces 0-3 as the source interface: tapered pivot seats 0 and 2 and pivot bores 1 and 3. Apply the mirrored cuts or equivalent coaxial holes locally to the shell at the new stand station. Preserve the original pivot geometry and avoid cutting into the internal cylindrical chamber, partitions, or vessel envelope.

Constrain or position the mirrored stand so its pivot bosses are coaxial with the newly created shell bores and its broad faces are parallel to those of the original stand. Check clearance to the main enclosure, rear feet, removable vessel, fascia, and power-cord exit. Do not fuse the stand to the shell unless the original F18 is fused; preserve the same assembly relationship as the source stand.

operations_plan.summary: Trim the lowest portions of the original and duplicated stands with one common horizontal cut so both supports terminate in coplanar flat feet suitable for a stable flat surface.

steps.description: Determine a global horizontal support plane normal to the semantic Z axis. Because no cut height is dimensioned, place the plane at the highest elevation that intersects only the lowest curved portion of both stands, leaves useful finite-width contact regions, and remains below the gray enclosure, rear feet, mounting arms, pivot bosses, and cord exit. Use the original F18 outer and inner U-shaped surfaces, faces 365 and 366, to preview the resulting chord width. The same single global plane must be used for both stand solids.

Apply a planar trim or subtractive half-space cut to the original F18 stand, removing all stand material below the support plane. Limit the operation to the lower U-shaped region represented by outer surface 365 and inner surface 366. Preserve the upper arms, side faces, top faces, pivot bosses, and mounting interfaces represented by faces 361-364 and 367-372. The new planar cut face becomes the original stand's flat foot.

Apply the identical support-plane trim to the mirrored stand created in OP2_STEP2. Reference the copied outer and inner U-shaped surfaces generated from source faces 365 and 366. Remove only material below the common plane so the new stand receives a flat foot geometrically coplanar with the original stand's foot.

Validate the finished support condition against a simulated infinite flat surface coincident with the cut plane. Confirm that both new planar foot faces contact the plane simultaneously, are parallel and coplanar within modeling tolerance, and are separated longitudinally enough to resist rocking. Check that no enclosure surface, rear foot, cord-exit hardware, or power cord lies below the intended support plane in the appliance's resting configuration. If interference exists, adjust the common plane upward only enough to clear it, then regenerate both trims together.
